                                                                  Abstract                                1. Introduction

                                             Long video understanding poses a significant challenge
                                         for current Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
                                         Notably, the MLLMs are constrained by their limited con-
                                         text lengths and the substantial costs while processing long
                                         videos. Although several existing methods attempt to re-
                                         duce visual tokens, their strategies encounter severe bot-
                                         tleneck, restricting MLLMs’ ability to perceive fine-grained
                                         visual details. In this work, we propose Video-XL, a novel
                                         approach that leverages MLLMs’ inherent key-value (KV)
                                         sparsification capacity to condense the visual input. Specif-
                                         ically, we introduce a new special token, the Visual Summa-
                                         rization Token (VST), for each interval of the video, which
                                         summarizes the visual information within the interval as
                                         its associated KV. The VST module is trained by instruc-         Figure 1. Video-XL achieves state-of-the-art results across several
                                         tion fine-tuning, where two optimizing strategies are offered.   video benchmarks, surpassing other models of comparable sizes.
                                         1. Curriculum learning, where VST learns to make small

                                         (easy) and large compression (hard) progressively. 2. Com-

                                         posite data curation, which integrates single-image, multi-
                                                                                                          augmenting large language models (LLMs) [33, 34, 40]

                                         pression granularity based on the information density of

Figure 2. Overview of Video-XL. The input data (single-image, multi-images, or video) is encoded and projected as visual tokens. The
visual tokens are dynamically split into intervals based on semantic consistency (measured by depth score). The visual information in each
interval is compressed as VSTs’ KVs, which enables MLLMs to perceive and understand longer inputs than its context window.

    Composite Data curation. Long-video instruction tun-            leverage GPT-4 to extract the key events and arrange them
ing data is very scarce in reality, which hinders the effective     in a temporal order. VICO requires models to identify and
training of Video-XL. To mitigate this problem, we propose          reason about key information in a long video, thereby en-
the composite curation of training data, where extra data re-       hancing their long video comprehension capabilities.
sources are introduced to enhance the training effect.

4.6. Ablation Studies                                                 Table 5. Analysis of training effect from different data.
We conducted extensive ablation studies to explore Video-
XL’s effectiveness regarding its compression mechanism,
training method, and data curation.
    Compression mechanism. First, we compare Video-XL
with previous common pre-compression methods, includ-
ing average pooling, Q-Former [15], LLaMA-VID [18],
LLaMA-Adapter [9], and C-Abstractor [2]. For a fair com-
parison, these methods are implemented based on their offi-
cial codes, but switched to the same architecture and train-
ing data as our method. With a uniform compression ratio
of 16×, we report the results on two long video bench-
marks, MLVU-test and VideoMME, as well as two pop-
ular VQA benchmarks, MME [7] and MMB [27]. As                              Figure 6. Analysis of training effect from VICO.
shown in Table 2, Video-XL significantly outperforms pre-
vious methods across all benchmarks, particularly on long        pression based on an interval of 1440 tokens. From the ex-
video benchmarks, which require fine-grained detail under-       periment results in Table 3, we can validate the effective-
standing and long-term relational reasoning. Additionally,       ness of our method, as it leads to a substantial improvement
Video-XL achieves high-fidelity compression with minimal         over the dynamic-compression disabled baselines. Mean-
performance loss, even at compression ratios as high as          while, we can also observe that it’s necessary to conduct
16×. Moreover, we further explore the performance un-            dynamic compression during training, as no improvements
der various compression ratios (2×, 8×,16×, 32×) in Fig-         are obtained if it’s only enabled for testing stage. More dis-
ure 5. Note that 32× is directly tested without fine-tuning.     cussions on this issue are provided in the supplementary.

a large margin. Meanwhile, it also effectively preserves its     tings: 1. using randomized compression ratios within 16×,

Figure 1. Video-XL can achieve better performance on long video   tential of visual compression, we developed an automated
benchmarks with increased context length.

   Discussion on the Generalization. We find that Video-          dataset called Visual Clue Order (VICO). In this section,
XL demonstrates strong generalization capabilities. On            we highlight its key features across several aspects.
one hand, the language compressor can be flexibly applied            Diversified Video Categories. VICO offers a compre-
across various language models. In addition to Qwen2, we          hensive collection of videos across various genres. Initially,
conducted experiments with Vicuna and LLaMA2, with re-            we source videos from CinePile, which includes movies,
sults shown in the Table 5. In the future, we plan to intro-      TV series, and cartoons. Additionally, we collect real-world
duce smaller language models to enable Video-XL to pro-           videos such as egocentric videos, documentaries, games,
cess longer videos on a single GPU. On the other hand,            sports, tutorials, and surveillance footage. The proportion
Video-XL requires only relatively short videos (under two         of each video type is illustrated in Figure 2.
minutes) for training but can handle videos nearly an hour           Versertile video length. VICO comprises videos of di-
long during inference. We believe this is largely due to          verse lengths, ranging from 1 minute to over 9 minutes, as
the design of both the training data and the model itself.        shown in Figure 3. Additionally, each video is annotated
In the training data, the model learns to understand long         with QA pairs for event/action ordering and detailed cap-
videos by leveraging images, multi-image sequences, and           tions for individual video clips. This allows MLLMs to
short video data. Furthermore, in the model’s architecture,       leverage the dataset to enhance their long video compre-

                                Prompt for VICO QA generation
              I will provide you with a series of video clip descriptions. Please summarize 4
              unique clues from these clips in sequence. Each clue should consist of sevral
              words and must be a unique event or action that only appears in one specific clip.
              Do not include objects, people, or places unless they are integral to describing
              an event or action. Ensure that the clues are distinct across all clips and are
              listed in the order they occur.
              Please return me the index of the clip and the clue.
              The output should be in JSON format as follows:
              {index1:"clue1", index2:"clue2", index3:"clue3",index4:"clue4"}
